# Export capability matrix

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:matrix` from v1/src/export/matrix.ts. Edit the code, not this file. -->

This is the project's central honest statement (design guide §3). The exporters consult the same data, and every export reports per property which of the four outcomes happened:

- **exact**: the target plays it identically.
- **approximated**: bounded error, e.g. `linear()` for a bounce. The error is reported.
- **baked**: replaced by extra keyframes within a tolerance. The report gives the count and the maximum deviation.
- **unrepresentable**: the target can't do it. It's clamped and you're warned.

| Capability | Lottie | CSS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Per-property keyframe times | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | CSS: translate/rotate/scale/opacity/colour are separate @keyframes. X and Y share `translate`. |
| Per-segment cubic-bezier easing | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | CSS: animation-timing-function inside the keyframe that starts the segment. |
| Per-dimension easing (X ≠ Y) | ✅ exact | ⚠️ baked | translate and scale are one property each; resampled and baked to tolerance. |
| Spatial bezier motion path | ✅ exact | ⚠️ baked | Baked to keyframes, or exact with the offset-path option (motion along a path). |
| Bounce / elastic / spring | ⚠️ baked | ≈ approximated | CSS: linear() with adaptive sampling. Lottie has only beziers: baked to keyframes. |
| Overshoot (y outside [0, 1]) | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | Legal in cubic-bezier() and linear(). |
| Handle x outside [0, 1] | ✅ exact | ❌ unrepresentable | cubic-bezier() requires x ∈ [0, 1]. Clamped, and reported. |
| Rotate-then-translate (orbital) order | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | Individual CSS properties are fixed T→R→S, so the orbit rotation goes on a wrapper element; Lottie uses a null parent. |
| Animated anchor point | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | left/top/transform-origin animate together in one @keyframes; per-dimension anchor easing is baked. |
| Drivers (property linked to another) | ⚠️ baked | ⚠️ baked | Neither target links properties without expressions; sampled to keyframes. |
| Hold / step keyframes | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | CSS: steps(1, end). |
| Perceptual (OKLab) colour interpolation | ⚠️ baked | ⚠️ baked | Both targets lerp sRGB; extra keyframes keep the path within ΔE 1. |
| Rotation beyond 360° | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | Stored unwrapped; both targets accumulate. |
| Layer parenting | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | CSS: nested elements. |
| Layer in/out points | ✅ exact | ✅ exact | CSS: a visibility animation with steps(1, end). |
| Keyframes between frames | ≈ approximated | ✅ exact | Legal in Lottie but many players round; the analysis reports the maximum shift. |

## Tolerances

| Baked value | Subdivision target (the report shows the measured maximum) |
|---|---|
| Position (curved paths, per-dimension easing) | 0.25 px (`tolerancePx` option) |
| Scale, rotation, opacity, anchor | 0.25 of the property's unit |
| Colour (OKLab → sRGB players) | ΔE (OKLab ×100) ≤ 1 |
| `linear()` easing | 0.002 of the eased range |
| Drivers | 0.1 of the property's unit |

## How it's verified

`npm run test:browser` renders the demo scene three ways at 30 times — our canvas preview, lottie-web (SVG renderer), and the exported CSS paused through the Web Animations API — and compares pixels. See [easing.md](easing.md) for the solver-vs-browser check.
